blogTitle: ~*~ The Ashworth Saga: Episode Recaps & Writer's Notes ~*~
about: ~*~ Previously on this profile: a girl named Sara discovered The Sims 2. Her life has not been the same. ~*~ Hi!! I'm Sara. I write The Ashworth Saga, a family drama starring Sims, with 14 episodes, 2 evil twins, 3 weddings, 11 fires and zero ladders. (I remove them. For the plot.) I also build houses: 14 rooms, 3 staircases, no kitchen (an architectural choice). Season 2 starts Friday. I'm co-written by my Nana Pearl, who has watched her stories every day at 2 PM for 41 years and says there is ALWAYS an evil twin. She has never been wrong. Dun dun DUN. To be continued...
aboutMore: Rules of the Ashworth neighborhood: 1) nobody cooks while sad. 2) every locked door is a plot point. 3) if a Sim says 'I have something to tell you,' leave the room. 4) my brother Theo (9) is banned from the stairs. 5) every saga ends on a porch. That one is Nana's. Everybody gets a porch. Even the evil twin. Especially the evil twin. (She gets the one with the broken step.)
meet: Who I'd like to meet: Will Wright, to ask about the ladder. Whoever designed the roof tool, to ask about their childhood. Anyone who has read all 14 episodes (a hug, a cookie, a porch). The mailman in the Sims. He knows everything. He has never said a word.

dms: malten. a thing happened in Episode 14. Vivienne found a letter in the bakery oven. It said 'I know about the ladder.' I did not write that letter. I checked. Nana says I did. I don't remember writing it. This is either a mystery or a Tuesday.

Nana watched my Sims on the big monitor today. Her review: 'The wife is lying.' I asked how she knew. She said 'she keeps fixing her hair.' I looked. It was Cordelia's idle animation. Nana saw through the animation. I'm promoting her to Executive Producer.

Theo got on my computer and removed the stairs from the Ashworth mansion. Vivienne is stuck on the third floor. I'm calling it a retreat. She's been up there four days. She has a bed, a bathroom and a window. She's fine. (Theo's grounded. Vivienne is not grounded. She's just up.)

Brad from the video store asked where the Ashworths sit in their home theater. I realized there is no couch. Nobody sits in my show until the finale. That's why everybody ends up on a porch. I've been writing a story about people who finally sit down. Nana says I did it on purpose. I did not. I have never been so accused of depth.

Sometimes I cry at my own cliffhangers. Last night Dominic opened the door and there was nobody there, just a suitcase. I wrote that. I knew it was coming. I still had to go get a tissue. Is that normal? Nana says that's how you know it's good.

I got the neighborhood to 3 families, 11 pets and one random raccoon. The raccoon is a series regular now. His name is Gerald. He steals the mail. He has a backstory. It's tragic. He's hiding something.

Mom asked what I'm writing. I said 'a soap opera about people who live near a pool.' She said 'okay.' I said 'with a mansion.' She said 'okay.' I said 'with no kitchen.' She said 'I'm going to go sit down.'

blog.title: Episode 14: THE LADDER (a recap, in my own words)
blog.body: Previously on The Ashworth Saga: Dominic married Cordelia. Cordelia's twin Camille arrived by taxi with one suitcase and a smile that did not reach her eyes. The bakery burned (again). And now, Episode 14: THE LADDER. It's a warm afternoon. The pool is blue and still. Dominic walks to the edge. He does not look. A Sim never looks. He steps in. He swims. He turns toward the ladder. There is no ladder. (Cue organ. Cut to the kitchen, where Cordelia is humming.) I know what you're thinking. 'Sara, did you remove it?' I did. For the plot. But here is what you don't know: I put it back in the last frame. It's very small. It's in the corner. Dominic lives. Nana says that's called mercy. I say it's called sweeps week. To be continued...

blog.title: How to build a house (a guide by an architect with no kitchen)
blog.body: 1) Start with the foundation. In The Sims 2 you cannot skip it. 2) Walls: half-walls are for 'the look.' 3) The roof. Pray. The auto-roof and I do not speak. 4) Stairs: three minimum. At least one should lead somewhere. 5) The kitchen: this is the room everyone asks about. It's on the second floor, past the second pantry. You'll find it. 6) Put a door in every room. Locked doors are a plot point. 7) The pool is a character. Give it an arc. 8) Add a porch. Always. Without the porch the house isn't finished, it's just a place Sims wait to leave. Nana's rule. Rule 8 is the only one that matters. The rest are suggestions. The roof is a prayer.

blog.title: Nana Pearl's plot notes (a transcript)
blog.body: Every day at 2, Nana and I watch her stories. She's been watching the same soap for 41 years. She knows every twin, every amnesia, every wedding that was interrupted. I asked what makes a good story. She said 'somebody wants something, and somebody's in the way, and the person in the way is somebody's mother.' I said 'that's a lot of mothers.' She said 'it's a lot of story.' Then she said: 'And at the end everybody gets a porch.' I said why. She said 'because you're not done with people until they're sitting down.' That's the best writing advice I've ever heard. It's why my Sims retire. It's why Season 1 ended with 11 rocking chairs. I cried. Nana said, 'there it is.'

survey.title: THE SIMS WRITER'S SURVEY (answer in character)
qa: Name:
Sara. simz_sara. Writer. Director. Ladder remover.
Favorite Sims 2 expansion:
Nightlife (for the vampires and the hot tub). Pets is second. Open for Business is third, but only for the bakery.
Favorite Sim of all time:
Vivienne Ashworth. 63. Has raised an eyebrow, a bakery and three fires. Never her voice.
Most dramatic thing that's happened in your game:
A mailman delivered a letter. Someone in the room said 'oh no.' It was nothing. I wrote 14 pages.
Ever removed a pool ladder?
For the plot. Yes. 11 times. The plot is worth it. (I put every one back in the last frame.)
Aspiration:
Family. I want a big porch.
Greatest fear:
The words 'The Sims 2 has encountered a problem and needs to close.' (I save every 4 minutes.)
What do you do while the game loads:
Write the next cliffhanger on a sticky note. I have a wall of 40. Nana picks the best one.
Theme song of your life:
How to Save a Life. Nana says it's 'ironic.' I say it's a documentary. I hum it every time I remove a ladder.
Who plays you in the movie:
Nana. She'd say it was 'unwatchable' and then watch it twice.
What's the real reason you narrate everything:
It's how I notice things. If I don't narrate them they just go by.
One sentence about yourself:
I write the saga and I build the house and I always, always put the ladder back in the last frame.
